survey: Image 4 is a round wall-style clock standing upright on a green floor, in front of a striped green wall. The camera is about level and turned slightly to the right of front-on. Because of that, the right side of the thick orange rim shows a little of its depth, and the rim reads as a slightly upright ellipse, about 0.94 as wide as it is tall. The white dial sits flush inside the rim and has the same slight squash, so the two rounds agree. The 12 hour markers and the minute dots run evenly around that ellipse and point at the centre. The 12 and 6 markers stay vertical, the 3 and 9 markers stay horizontal, and the slight horizontal squash is the same on both sides. The hour, minute and second hands all pivot on one central hub that faces the camera like the dial. The bottom of the rim rests on the floor just in front of the wall line, with a soft contact shadow beneath it. The floor is seen from slightly above, which fits a nearly level camera looking a little down at a clock this size.
